Run the scenarios under both versions

Source: R/run.R
run_scenarios.Rd

Each run is a fresh R process (via callr) whose library path starts with that version's library; the run checks that the package was loaded from there. With order = "abba" the runs go base, candidate, candidate, base, so drift in machine load hits both versions alike, and each version runs twice so that steps whose results differ between two runs of the same version (unseeded randomness) are found.

Usage

run_scenarios(
  d,
  force = FALSE,
  timeout = Inf,
  step_timeout = 300,
  workers = 1L,
  quiet = FALSE
)

Arguments

d

A dossier(); its settings say how the runs are made.

force

Repeat runs even when their results are up to date.

timeout

Seconds one run (one version, all scenarios) may take before it is stopped, which stops run_scenarios() with the end of the run's log. (A step that crashes R is recorded and skipped; see below.)

step_timeout

Seconds one execution of a step may take: its captured run, or one of its timed repeats. A step that takes longer is stopped and recorded as an error, "timed out after N s", and the run goes on with the next step: the run's process is stopped and started again from a fresh run folder, skipping that step, so every step before it runs again and the steps after it in its scenario run without what it would have created. The version's other run does not start the step again once this run has finished. A notice comes at half the limit. The default of 300 s is far beyond what a vignette chunk or an example normally takes, so it catches only steps that hang; Inf sets no limit. A step during which the run's R process dies (a segfault in compiled code, a call to quit()) is recorded as an error, "R stopped in this step", with the reason R gave, and the run goes on the same way: the process is started again and the step skipped. A step whose output pkgdossier itself fails to capture is recorded the same way, with R's message. A process that dies outside any step stops the run with the end of its log. The run plan lists, per run, the steps that timed out or crashed, and how many runs went at once while it ran.

workers

How many runs may go at once (a whole number). Runs that went at the same time competed for the machine, so their timings are shown but no step is labelled slower or faster; use it when the timings do not matter (a quick check in CI, reps = 0). ABBA order is kept: base and candidate run together, then candidate and base.

quiet

Suppress progress messages: a plan line, each run's end (and, after the first, an estimate of the time left), notices about slow steps, and outside an interactive session a line every minute.

Value

The run plan (a data frame with one row per run), invisibly.

Details

Per step the run keeps the console transcript (output and messages, in order), the printed form of visible values, warnings and errors with their classes, the numbers and element names of the values (for steps with values = TRUE), plots as PNG files at the step's figure size, the elapsed and CPU time of the captured run and, for timed steps, reps more timings. The seed is set as the dossier's reseed says, and timed repeats start from the random-number state of the step's captured run.

Scenarios run one after another in the same process, but each starts from the same session state: options, attached packages, environment variables, the colour palette, the random-number kind and the working directory that one scenario sets are put back before the next. Graphics parameters cannot leak (each step draws on its own device); namespaces a scenario loads stay loaded.

Paths and memory addresses change from run to run: in what a step prints, warns or returns as text, the session's temporary folder is written <tempdir>, the run's folder <run>, a temporary file name (as tempfile() makes, also bare, as dir(tempdir()) lists it) <tempfile>, and an address (a formula's <environment: 0x55e7ad2f3268>, or 0x and 8 to 16 hex digits as tracemem() and data.table's address() show them) 0x<address>, so a step that shows one still compares. A system.time() or proc.time() result a step shows as its value, or keeps in a variable, is left out of its printed output and numbers: it differs in every run, and the runner times each step itself. One printed inside another object or with an explicit print(), and output a package prints about its own timings, still differ, and the step is reported as unstable.

Vignette scenarios run from a fresh copy of the baseline's vignettes/ folder, so code that reads a file shipped next to the vignette finds it; scenario-file scenarios run from the run's own folder.

The scenarios are resolved once (from the baseline's vignettes, help pages and the scenario files) and saved in the work folder, so every run sees identical code. A run whose results already exist is reused unless force = TRUE, as long as nothing that shapes its results has changed: the installed version, the scenarios' code, the dossier's run settings (reps, seed, reseed, language, width, dpi, caps, skip_classes, deps), R, the versions of the packages that version and its scenarios load (and of evaluate, which captures them), and pkgdossier's runner. The installs must match the dossier: after changing its dependencies, or R, call prepare_versions() first. After fixing the candidate and calling prepare_versions() again, only the candidate's runs are repeated. A run is also reused under a new step_timeout when its own limit was the same, or lower with no step stopped by it.

Examples

# \donttest{
d <- example_dossier()
prepare_versions(d, quiet = TRUE)
run_scenarios(d)
#> Running 3 scenario(s), 30 steps, under udfixture 1.0.0 and 1.1.0 in 4 runs (abba), 3 timed repeats per timed step; a step's run stops after 300 s (step_timeout)
#> Machine before: CPU 0% busy, 0 other R processes
#> [1/4] base_a: up to date, reused
#> [2/4] cand_a: up to date, reused
#> [3/4] cand_b: up to date, reused
#> [4/4] base_b: up to date, reused
# }
